statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-47240 (GHSA-8p34-64r3-mwg8): Net::IMAP raw data arguments (criteria for search and uid_search, search keys for sort, thread, uid_sort and uid_thread, and attr for fetch and uid_fetch) can embed non-synchronizing literals, which net-imap sends without checking that the server supports them; a server without LITERAL+, LITERAL- or IMAP4rev2 support may read the literal's contents as new pipelined commands, allowing IMAP command injection: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/security/advisories/GHSA-8p34-64r3-mwg8. The advisory lists fixes in 0.5.15 and 0.6.4.1; on the 0.4 release line it is fixed in net-imap 0.4.25, whose release notes list CVE-2026-47240 (https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/releases/tag/v0.4.25), by https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/commit/7228b22b81a49198172fb111a343fef80236bbf5 (a backport of https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/pull/701, merged in https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/pull/707), which makes send_literal in lib/net/imap/command_data.rb refuse a non-synchronizing literal unless the server advertises support for it. The DHI ruby-3.3 package for Alpine 3.23 is published as 3.3.10-r0, 3.3.10-r1, 3.3.11-r1, 3.3.11-r2, 3.3.11-r3, 3.3.12-r3, 3.3.13-r3, 3.3.14-r3 and 3.3.14-r4 on x86_64 and aarch64 (ruby-3.3-libs and ruby-3.3-full 3.3.11-r1 are published for aarch64 only), as listed in the repository index on 2026-11-27. net-imap is not in the ruby-3.3 package itself: it is installed by the ruby3.3-net-imap gem package, built from the same source but carrying the gem's version, which ruby-3.3-full depends on. The range below is written in the ruby-3.3 package's own versions, so each ruby-3.3 build is placed by the net-imap release its build installs. We downloaded every published ruby3.3-net-imap package (0.4.21-r0, 0.4.21-r1, 0.4.21-r2, 0.4.21-r3, 0.4.25-r3 and 0.4.25-r4) and every published ruby-3.3-libs package for both architectures, each checked against its repository index checksum, and compared each installed net-imap lib directory with the release from rubygems.org: 0.4.21-r0 to 0.4.21-r2 are identical to net-imap 0.4.21, 0.4.21-r3 (despite its label) is identical to net-imap 0.4.24, and 0.4.25-r3 and 0.4.25-r4 are identical to net-imap 0.4.25. The repository index records the same build commit for ruby3.3-net-imap 0.4.21-r3 and ruby-3.3 3.3.11-r3, so 3.3.11-r3 is the build that replaced Ruby 3.3.11's bundled net-imap 0.4.21 with 0.4.24. Ruby 3.3.10 and 3.3.11 bundle net-imap 0.4.21 and Ruby 3.3.12, 3.3.13 and 3.3.14 bundle 0.4.25 (https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/v3_3_11/gems/bundled_gems, https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/v3_3_12/gems/bundled_gems), so 3.3.10-r0 to 3.3.11-r2 ship net-imap 0.4.21, 3.3.11-r3 ships 0.4.24, and 3.3.12-r3 onward ship 0.4.25. No ruby-3.3-libs build installs net-imap; ruby-3.3-libs 3.3.11-r3 only carries a cached copy of the net-imap 0.4.24 gem archive (usr/lib/ruby/gems/3.3.0/cache/net-imap-0.4.24.gem, identical to the rubygems.org file), which Ruby does not load. The installed lib/net/imap/command_data.rb carries that check (the error 'Cannot send non-synchronizing literal without known server support') in the 0.4.25 copies and not in the 0.4.21 or 0.4.24 copies. Both architectures agree for every build. So every ruby-3.3 build before 3.3.12-r3 ships net-imap without this fix, and 3.3.12-r3 and every later build ship net-imap 0.4.25: the range is fixed at 3.3.12-r3.

CVE-2026-47240 (GHSA-8p34-64r3-mwg8): before net-imap 0.5.15 and 0.6.4.1, the raw-data arguments of search, uid_search, sort, uid_sort, thread, uid_thread, fetch and uid_fetch can carry non-synchronizing literals without checking that the server supports them, and a server without that support may run the literal's contents as new pipelined commands (command injection); before 0.5.14 and 0.6.4 these arguments were not validated at all: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/security/advisories/GHSA-8p34-64r3-mwg8. On the 0.5 release line it is fixed in net-imap 0.5.15, whose release notes name this advisory: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/releases/tag/v0.5.15. In the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, net-imap ships in the ruby3.4-net-imap package, which is built from the ruby-3.4 source with its own version number; ruby-3.4-full depends on it. We downloaded every published ruby3.4-net-imap package for Alpine 3.23 on x86_64 and aarch64, checked each against its repository index checksum, and compared its installed lib directory with the net-imap release from rubygems.org; each matches its release byte for byte: 0.5.8-r0 and 0.5.8-r1 install net-imap 0.5.8, 0.5.8-r2 installs net-imap 0.5.14, and 0.5.15-r2, 0.5.15-r3 and 0.5.15-r4 install net-imap 0.5.15. Each ruby-3.4 build is built together with the ruby3.4-net-imap package of the same package release (-rN): 3.4.8-r0 to 3.4.9-r1 with net-imap 0.5.8 (ruby3.4-net-imap 0.5.8-r0 and 0.5.8-r1); 3.4.9-r2, which upgrades the bundled net-imap to 0.5.14, with ruby3.4-net-imap 0.5.8-r2; and 3.4.10-r2 and every later build, whose Ruby releases bundle net-imap 0.5.15, with ruby3.4-net-imap 0.5.15-r2 to 0.5.15-r4 (0.5.15-r2 was published with ruby-3.4 3.4.10-r2). The published DHI Ruby 3.4.9 and 3.4.10 dev images for Alpine 3.23 install ruby-3.4 3.4.9-r2 with ruby3.4-net-imap 0.5.8-r2 (net-imap 0.5.14) and ruby-3.4 3.4.10-r3 with ruby3.4-net-imap 0.5.15-r3 (net-imap 0.5.15), on amd64 and arm64. The ruby-3.4-libs 3.4.9-r2 package also carries the net-imap 0.5.14 gem archive, identical to the rubygems.org file; ruby-3.4-libs 3.4.9-r1 carries none. So the first published ruby-3.4 build that ships the fix is 3.4.10-r2: the builds before it ship net-imap 0.5.8 or 0.5.14, and it and every later build ship net-imap 0.5.15.
